shipped_rows.title_o: Deficient host-bacteria interactions in inflammatory bowel disease? The toll-like receptor (TLR)-4 Asp299gly polymorphism is associated with Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis
shipped_rows.authors_o: Franchimont; Vermeire; El Housni; Pierik; Van Steen; Gustot; Quertinmont; Abramowicz; Van Gossum; Devière; Rutgeerts

blind_target.authors: Karban AS, Okazaki T, Panhuysen CI, Gallegos T, Potter JJ, Bailey-Wilson JE et al.
blind_target.title: Functional annotation of a novel NFKB1 promoter polymorphism that increases risk for ulcerative colitis.
blind_target.evidence_quote: We first set out to confirm the published associations of , susceptibility to CD or UC with NFKB1 and TLR4 alleles. Specifically, we attempted to replicate the putative association of the -94delATTG allele of NFKB1 (NFKB1 94delATTG) with UC and the 299Gly allele of TLR4 (TLR4299G1y) with CD and UC.24,25
blind_target.outcome_quote: In terms of the putative NFKB1 94delATTG risk allele, Karban et al.25 first reported an association with risk of developing UC. We therefore tested this specific hypothesis in our entire set of samples but did not find significant evidence of association (OR = 0.99, 95% CI: 0.81-1.2; Supplementary Table 2).
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The paper’s own samples did not support the original UC association; the pooled literature finding is not the outcome of the new-sample replication.

prior_decision.reason: This is an omitted target: the paper explicitly re-tests the ulcerative colitis association of NFKB1 -94delATTG reported by Karban et al. (2004) in its new sample cohorts and finds no significant evidence of association.

luna_triage.reason: Results explicitly say the authors tested the specific ulcerative-colitis risk hypothesis attributed to Karban et al. in their sample and found no significant association. The sole supplied shipped row is Franchimont et al. on TLR4, a distinct original.
